Tammy Taylor 2

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The end of the Tammy Taylor franchise - is this the final nail in the coffin?

Unique Selling Point:
Tammy Taylor USA has sent Mel & Peet Viljoen a Notice to terminate the Master License Agreement within 30 days, if they do not comply with a full audit requested in October 2020. The notice was issued on 18 February 2021 and the 30 days notice period expires on Sunday 21st March 2021.
Will Peet & Mel comply and avert disaster, or will they continue to ignore Tammy Taylor USA's demands, thereby making all their existing franchisee agreements invalid, preventing the use of any Tammy Taylor logos or products and pushing the 48 store holders into certain financial ruin.

Summary:
After our first exposé in August 2020, Tammy Taylor USA's lawyers sent Mel & Peet Viljoen a Notice of Audit in September 2020. They were given until 30 October to comply:
Pursuant to Section 3.7 of the Agreement. Licensor is conducting an audit of your operations under the Agreement and hereby demands that you produce all business and personal records, bank statements, financial statements, tax returns, financial statistics, reports and any other relevant document and data containing true, accurate and complete information.
Not only was this demand ignored,Mel & Peet continued to sell franchise licenses to would-be store owners. A stated in our previous programme they have sold over 300 licenses, yet only 48 stores are operational. Franchise opportunities are marketed aggressively, yet the products are not. Many believe that their real business is selling the dream, and not following up. We have 3 case studies who bought into the dream, but never opened a store.





Further information:
Mel & Peet's lawyer is Ruann Kruger. He sat in on first interview with Mel, and answered all the questions on her behalf. He bought the Groenkoof store (the subject of our first story) which was being run by his wife. Recently this store was sold to celebrity Lerato Kganyago, who announced it on Twitter on 4 March 2021, with the comment: "Still feels unreal. Black Child your Dreams are valid. I'm officially a Franchise owner."
As Peet and Mel's trusted lawyer, there is no doubt that Ruann Kruger has sold the Groenkloof store with the full knowledge that Tammy Taylor USA is about to cancel the Master License Agreement, thereby cancelling any value in owning a Tammy Taylor franchise in South Africa.

1. Lea Abvajee - in December 2018 she invested R345 000 into Tammy Taylor Nails SA to operate in the Fairland area. In January a 'location specialist' was assigned to find her premises. Despite both verbal & written promises from Peet & Mel nothing materialised for over a year.Peet assured her that if she didn't have premises by the end of Feb 2020 he would remind her. On 6 march he then offered her The Marc in Sandton. Lea knew that this store already belonged to someone else, and sent Peet a cancellation letter and demanded a refund. A year later, nothing has been forthcoming, hence her interaction with Tammy Taylor USA.

2. Santhuri Poovalingam - went for interview with Peet in 2018, said she wanted a store in Sandton CBD, preferably The Marc. She too paid R345 000 franchise fee but was told The Marc was not available.. After a year she was told The Marc had been sold to someone else, and she still had no store. When she realised they were opening several stores in Sandton within a 2km radius she decided the business wasn't for her. The Viljoens have ignored all her demands for a refund of the franchise fee, even a letter of summons sent a year ago.

3. Yashna Chetty - Attended a franchise meeting with Peet Viljoen on 19 January 2021. Had not seen the Carte Blanche story as it is no longer on YouTube. She was completely sold on the concept and Peet kept reassuring her that she could get a full refund of the license fee. She paid R345 000 that same day. No License agreement was signed. The next day she called Jenelle at The Marc to ask about the business. Jenelle told her to run for the hills. On 21st January she instructed her bank to reverse the payment. The money had already been transferred out of Tammy Taylor's account. On 25th January she sent TT an letter, and drove to Head Office to deliver it stating she was cancelling the agreement within the cooling off period. They ignored her. On 4th February she met with Mel and Ruann Kruger (lawyer) He then wrote to her that they would first have to resell her chosen location before they could refund her. But she hadn't chosen a location and no License Agreement was signed. She has sent them a lawyer's letter of demand which they have ignored. When she escalated this to Tammy Taylor USA, they sent her copies of the lawyers letters re the Audit and the Termination of the Master License.

Extra Budget Items:
Ideally we should get an intern to apply to be a Tammy Taylor franchisee, and go to a meeting with Peet Viljoen, to get his sales pitch and reassurance that the franchise license fee is fully refundable.

Press Release:


Nail Care Brand Out of Shape

The dream was to buy into an internationally-renowned nailcare franchise. But after investing millions into this business venture, some investors got nothing out. Last year, we revealed the financial losses and broken promises that investors suffered at the hands of the owners who had raked in millions from their franchisees. Now, Carte Blanche investigates why the American Licensor threatened to terminate the Master License Agreement for the South African company when they failed to comply with an audit.

Producer: Kate Barry | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


TAMMY TAYLOR 2

V/O: In August last year Carte Blanche exposed the hard reality beneath the polished veneer of international franchise business, Tammy Taylor Nails.

Jennelle: If I had to turn back the hands of time, I would have definitely not bought into this franchise.

Taryn: It’s derailed my entire life.

Ntombi: I feel like I’m about to lose everything that I’ve invested.

Daniella: It was the worst experience of my life.

V/O: The local franchisors are Mel Viljoen, and her husband Peet, a disgraced lawyer who was struck off the roll in 2011. Local franchisees detailed how they lost millions when stock was withheld, refunds were withheld and their stores were simply confiscated and resold. But Mel Viljoen denied they had done anything wrong and vowed to continue with their business model.

Mel: We’re going to keep selling franchises, we’re going to keep taking over stores if people don’t pay their fees. That is just the way business is.

Link: After our last story many more case studies came forward to share their experiences of Tammy Taylor Nails South Africa. These are women who bought franchise licenses but never got to open a store. Hundreds of thousands of Rands paid out with nothing to show for it. No cash and no cachet.

V/O: Wedding and events planner Lea Abvajee bought a franchise license in December 2018 for R345 000.

Lea: At the time I was interested in the Fairlands area which was an area that was developing, it was growing.

V/O: But the Tammy Taylor location specialist couldn't secure premises in the Fairlands or Northcliff area. As the months dragged by Abvajee became concerned when she heard nothing from Head Office. In December 2019 she sent the Viljoens a message.

Lea: You know what guys, it’s a year down the line. No locations have been secured. I am waiting to open up a salon. Peet immediately gave me a call. He actually said this verbatim that ‘Lea if I do not find you a store by the end of February 2020, I’m going to pay you your money back.

Masa: And still…no money back?

Lea: Still no money back.

Masa: At this point had you signed a contract?

Lea: There was no contract. I had never signed a contract with Tammy Taylor Nails South Africa.

V/O: That was a mistake, according to business growth expert Pavlo Phitidis.

Pavlo: In any instance where you pay money over before you have signed an agreement, especially in business, you’re going to open yourself up to all sorts of bad behaviour that follows.

V/O: In March 2020 Abvajee finally asked for her money back but her request was ignored. She then went the legal route.

Lea: They do not respond to my lawyer. And again it’s a classic case of ignore, ignore, ignore.

Link: We asked Mel Viljoen for an interview and sent her a list of questions. Instead we got this Tammy Taylor media statement. They didn’t answer any of our questions, claiming that our August 2020 interview with them was biased, so they will refrain from any interaction with Carte Blanche going forward.

V/O: The only solution Mel Viljoen ever offered Abvajee, was to invest her license fee into another Tammy Taylor store in Witbank, that the owner allegedly abandoned.

Mel: She literally just walked away. Because they buy big salons and then they can’t, they have other stuff going on and then they just…it’s an African thing. I promise you, it’s just an African thing. And it’s not wrong. It’s not necessarily right or wrong, it’s just sometimes the way that it is.
Lea: Ja…

Mel: But that seems to be a trend amongst them.

Lea: I was absolutely angered by those comments against African women, because I am an African woman. So to say that they like to start things that they cannot finish, or they abandon things, you are speaking about me. You are speaking about me, my legacy, my heritage, my ancestry, that we are non-starters. We are not non-starters at all.

Link: I really wanted to ask Mel what exactly she meant by “it’s an African thing’. Unfortunately, that’s another question that was ignored.

V/O: In 2018 Santhuri Poovalingam also bought a franchise license for R345 000.

Santhuri: My first preference was the Sandton area, the Sandton CBD and Morningside area. When I did inquire there was nobody else interested in that vicinity.

V/O: She had her sights set on The Marc shopping centre but was told there was nothing available there. So she managed to secure premises about a kilometre away at the MyCiti centre in Morningside which is still under construction.

Santhuri: After I had paid the franchise fee I was then told a few months later that another lady had purchased at The Marc. And according to the blanket franchise agreement it was stipulated that they would not open a franchise within a 2-kilometre radius unless it was a major shopping centre as defined.

V/O: Although Tammy Taylor claimed The Marc was a major shopping centre, Santhuri Poovalingam decided to call it a day and ask for a refund. She’s still waiting.

Santhuri: We have sent them demand letters. The sheriff has issued them with a summons. However they have not defended it as yet.

Link: It seems that all requests for a refund were ignored, and even the Sheriff’s summons was ignored - as if Santhuri’s investment doesn’t matter, as if she herself is of no consequence. Again, all our questions about this were ignored

Pavlo: A legal summons has the opportunity to completely collapse a business. Whether you believe it's legitimate or not, good corporate governance, good ethical practice says you address it immediately.

V/O: This young franchisee has asked us to protect her identity, so we shall call her Jessica. In January this year she was invited to Tammy Taylor Head office for a meeting. Peet Viljoen’s sales pitch was so impressive that she decided there and then to buy a franchise.

Jessica: They handed me an invoice for the franchise fee. And they kept reassuring me in that meeting that the franchise fee is one hundred percent refundable.

V/O: But the day after she paid things changed.

Jessica: So suddenly different locations were being offered, and the locations I was interested in were not offered anymore. And so immediately I approached my bank and asked my bank if they could do a digital recall of the funds that had been paid because I had done an electronic transfer of the money.

V/O: But the bank could not reverse payment because there were insufficient funds in the Tammy Taylor account.

Pavlo: Investing a penny into a franchise before you’ve seen the Disclosure document, and before you yourself have spoken to franchisees to understand how does the Disclosure document translate into behaviour from the franchisor, is not doing your job properly as an investor.

V/O: But, Jessica then formally cancelled the deal within the prescribed cooling off period.

Jessica: Within 5 days after paying my money to them, I wrote them a formal letter requesting my money back.

Masa: Did they come back to you?

Jessica: No they didn’t. I didn’t receive a response from them. I then tried calling them and everything just went cold.

Pavlo: The Consumer Protection Act specifies very clearly that you’ve got a 10-day cooling off period, and any franchise agreement has to be aligned to the Consumer Protection Act….

V/O: Jessica then reached out to Tammy Taylor in the USA for help. They replied with a bombshell.

Jessica: They have given Tammy Taylor Nails South Africa notice to terminate the master license agreement between Peet and Melanie Viljoen and Tammy Taylor Nail's USA. And they sent me two letters.

V/O: The first letter was a Notice of Audit, requesting copies of bank statements, financial statements, tax returns, contracts and other documents.

Link: Peet and Mel Viljoen were given until the end of October last year to comply with the Audit. Guess what they did? They ignored it. For four months they didn’t respond to this demand from Tammy Taylor in the USA. And then things got serious.

V/O: The second letter was dated 18th of February 2021. Tammy Taylor in the USA gave the Viljoens a Notice of Termination of the Master License Agreement, giving them 30-days-notice of their intention to terminate the master license, unless they comply with the audit within that period.

Pavlo: No listen, that's pretty serious. It would imply that I have breached some of my obligations. And a letter like that would only typically come through if I have failed to meet those obligations, it would suggest a pretty material breach. What’s the most valuable commodity in commerce? Trust.

V/O: The 30 days have come and gone, and yet they still haven’t cured the breach with Tammy Taylor. A message from their lawyer Ruann Kruger confirms “we are currently in negotiations with her Attorneys to come to an agreement on when and how the required audit should be done.”

Link: Peet and Mel Viljoens actions don’t just affect their business, but the actions of their licensees as well. According to the Tammy Taylor website there are now 46 franchise stores in South Africa. That represents a substantial investment by dozens of women who stand to lose everything should the Master License Agreement be terminated.
V/O: In their media statement the Viljoens dismiss the email Jessica received from Tammy Taylor USA as “a falsified document”.
They also claim recent communication confirms the continuation of their Distribution Agreement. But the heavily redacted letter they provided did not confirm this at all.
So we asked for confirmation from the original letter. Instead they provided copies of recent stock orders placed and shipped to South Africa as proof.
But they also claim there has never been any intention to terminate the business relationship between them and Tammy Taylor USA
Text: The business relationship between Tammy Taylor Nails SA and Tammy Taylor USA is set in stone and there has never been any intention from either party to discontinue the relationship.
V/O: That’s clearly not true, so we decided to visit the Viljoens and show them the 30-Day Notice of Termination Letter.
Masa: We are looking for Peet or Mel Viljoen. Are they around?
Guy: No.
Masa: Do you know when they’ll be in?
Guy: No.
Lea: As strong women, as empowered women, as intelligent women, as African women we are not going to simply abandon, or simply back away We do not condone that. We are strong and we will see this thing through.

So she managed to secure premises about a kilometre away at the MyCiti centre in Morningside which is still under construction. Santhuri: After I had paid the franchise fee I was then told a few months later that another lady had purchased at The Marc. And according to the blanket franchise agreement it was stipulated that they would not open a franchise within a 2-kilometre radius unless it was a major shopping centre as defined. V/O: Although Tammy Taylor claimed The Marc was a major shopping centre, Santhuri Poovalingam decided to call it a day and ask for a refund. She’s still waiting. Santhuri: We have sent them demand letters. The sheriff has issued them with a summons. However they have not defended it as yet. Link: It seems that all requests for a refund were ignored, and even the Sheriff’s summons was ignored - as if Santhuri’s investment doesn’t matter, as if she herself is of no consequence. Again, all our questions about this were ignored Pavlo: A legal summons has the opportunity to completely collapse a business. Whether you believe it's legitimate or not, good corporate governance, good ethical practice says you address it immediately. V/O: This young franchisee has asked us to protect her identity, so we shall call her Jessica. In January this year she was invited to Tammy Taylor Head office for a meeting. Peet Viljoen’s sales pitch was so impressive that she decided there and then to buy a franchise. Jessica: They handed me an invoice for the franchise fee. And they kept reassuring me in that meeting that the franchise fee is one hundred percent refundable. V/O: But the day after she paid things changed. Jessica: So suddenly different locations were being offered, and the locations I was interested in were not offered anymore. And so immediately I approached my bank and asked my bank if they could do a digital recall of the funds that had been paid because I had done an electronic transfer of the money. V/O: But the bank could not reverse payment because there were insufficient funds in the Tammy Taylor account. Pavlo: Investing a penny into a franchise before you’ve seen the Disclosure document, and before you yourself have spoken to franchisees to understand how does the Disclosure document translate into behaviour from the franchisor, is not doing your job properly as an investor. V/O: But, Jessica then formally cancelled the deal within the prescribed cooling off period. Jessica: Within 5 days after paying my money to them, I wrote them a formal letter requesting my money back. Masa: Did they come back to you? Jessica: No they didn’t. I didn’t receive a response from them. I then tried calling them and everything just went cold. Pavlo: The Consumer Protection Act specifies very clearly that you’ve got a 10-day cooling off period, and any franchise agreement has to be aligned to the Consumer Protection Act…. V/O: Jessica then reached out to Tammy Taylor in the USA for help. They replied with a bombshell. Jessica: They have given Tammy Taylor Nails South Africa notice to terminate the master license agreement between Peet and Melanie Viljoen and Tammy Taylor Nail's USA. And they sent me two letters. V/O: The first letter was a Notice of Audit, requesting copies of bank statements, financial statements, tax returns, contracts and other documents. Link: Peet and Mel Viljoen were given until the end of October last year to comply with the Audit. Guess what they did? They ignored it. For four months they didn’t respond to this demand from Tammy Taylor in the USA. And then things got serious. V/O: The second letter was dated 18th of February 2021. Tammy Taylor in the USA gave the Viljoens a Notice of Termination of the Master License Agreement, giving them 30-days-notice of their intention to terminate the master license, unless they comply with the audit within that period. Pavlo: No listen, that's pretty serious. It would imply that I have breached some of my obligations. And a letter like that would only typically come through if I have failed to meet those obligations, it would suggest a pretty material breach. What’s the most valuable commodity in commerce? Trust. V/O: The 30 days have come and gone, and yet they still haven’t cured the breach with Tammy Taylor. A message from their lawyer Ruann Kruger confirms “we are currently in negotiations with her Attorneys to come to an agreement on when and how the required audit should be done.” Link: Peet and Mel Viljoens actions don’t just affect their business, but the actions of their licensees as well. According to the Tammy Taylor website there are now 46 franchise stores in South Africa. That represents a substantial investment by dozens of women who stand to lose everything should the Master License Agreement be terminated. V/O: In their media statement the Viljoens dismiss the email Jessica received from Tammy Taylor USA as “a falsified document”. They also claim recent communication confirms the continuation of their Distribution Agreement. But the heavily redacted letter they provided did not confirm this at all. So we asked for confirmation from the original letter. Instead they provided copies of recent stock orders placed and shipped to South Africa as proof. But they also claim there has never been any intention to terminate the business relationship between them and Tammy Taylor USA Text: The business relationship between Tammy Taylor Nails SA and Tammy Taylor USA is set in stone and there has never been any intention from either party to discontinue the relationship. V/O: That’s clearly not true, so we decided to visit the Viljoens and show them the 30-Day Notice of Termination Letter. Masa: We are looking for Peet or Mel Viljoen. Are they around? Guy: No. Masa: Do you know when they’ll be in? Guy: No. Lea: As strong women, as empowered women, as intelligent women, as African women we are not going to simply abandon, or simply back away We do not condone that. We are strong and we will see this thing through. Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Tammy Taylor 2 (5883) Kate Barry 18 May 2021

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): The end of the Tammy Taylor franchise - is this the final nail in the coffin?
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Tammy Taylor USA has sent Mel & Peet Viljoen a Notice to terminate the Master License Agreement within 30 days, if they do not comply with a full audit requested in October 2020. The notice was issued on 18 February 2021 and the 30 days notice period expires on Sunday 21st March 2021. Will Peet & Mel comply and avert disaster, or will they continue to ignore Tammy Taylor USA's demands, thereby making all their existing franchisee agreements invalid, preventing the use of any Tammy Taylor logos or products and pushing the 48 store holders into certain financial ruin.
metadata.Summary: After our first exposé in August 2020, Tammy Taylor USA's lawyers sent Mel & Peet Viljoen a Notice of Audit in September 2020. They were given until 30 October to comply: Pursuant to Section 3.7 of the Agreement. Licensor is conducting an audit of your operations under the Agreement and hereby demands that you produce all business and personal records, bank statements, financial statements, tax returns, financial statistics, reports and any other relevant document and data containing true, accurate and complete information. Not only was this demand ignored,Mel & Peet continued to sell franchise licenses to would-be store owners. A stated in our previous programme they have sold over 300 licenses, yet only 48 stores are operational. Franchise opportunities are marketed aggressively, yet the products are not. Many believe that their real business is selling the dream, and not following up. We have 3 case studies who bought into the dream, but never opened a store.
metadata.Further information: Mel & Peet's lawyer is Ruann Kruger. He sat in on first interview with Mel, and answered all the questions on her behalf. He bought the Groenkoof store (the subject of our first story) which was being run by his wife. Recently this store was sold to celebrity Lerato Kganyago, who announced it on Twitter on 4 March 2021, with the comment: "Still feels unreal. Black Child your Dreams are valid. I'm officially a Franchise owner." As Peet and Mel's trusted lawyer, there is no doubt that Ruann Kruger has sold the Groenkloof store with the full knowledge that Tammy Taylor USA is about to cancel the Master License Agreement, thereby cancelling any value in owning a Tammy Taylor franchise in South Africa. 1. Lea Abvajee - in December 2018 she invested R345 000 into Tammy Taylor Nails SA to operate in the Fairland area. In January a 'location specialist' was assigned to find her premises. Despite both verbal & written promises from Peet & Mel nothing materialised for over a year.Peet assured her that if she didn't have premises by the end of Feb 2020 he would remind her. On 6 march he then offered her The Marc in Sandton. Lea knew that this store already belonged to someone else, and sent Peet a cancellation letter and demanded a refund. A year later, nothing has been forthcoming, hence her interaction with Tammy Taylor USA. 2. Santhuri Poovalingam - went for interview with Peet in 2018, said she wanted a store in Sandton CBD, preferably The Marc. She too paid R345 000 franchise fee but was told The Marc was not available.. After a year she was told The Marc had been sold to someone else, and she still had no store. When she realised they were opening several stores in Sandton within a 2km radius she decided the business wasn't for her. The Viljoens have ignored all her demands for a refund of the franchise fee, even a letter of summons sent a year ago. 3. Yashna Chetty - Attended a franchise meeting with Peet Viljoen on 19 January 2021. Had not seen the Carte Blanche story as it is no longer on YouTube. She was completely sold on the concept and Peet kept reassuring her that she could get a full refund of the license fee. She paid R345 000 that same day. No License agreement was signed. The next day she called Jenelle at The Marc to ask about the business. Jenelle told her to run for the hills. On 21st January she instructed her bank to reverse the payment. The money had already been transferred out of Tammy Taylor's account. On 25th January she sent TT an letter, and drove to Head Office to deliver it stating she was cancelling the agreement within the cooling off period. They ignored her. On 4th February she met with Mel and Ruann Kruger (lawyer) He then wrote to her that they would first have to resell her chosen location before they could refund her. But she hadn't chosen a location and no License Agreement was signed. She has sent them a lawyer's letter of demand which they have ignored. When she escalated this to Tammy Taylor USA, they sent her copies of the lawyers letters re the Audit and the Termination of the Master License.
